evidence.field: hanzi.etymology_notes[1]
evidence.text: Phonosemantic compound. 日 represents the meaning and 生 represents the sound.

evidence.field: hanzi.etymology_notes[2]
evidence.text:
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *sleːŋ): phonetic 晶 (OC *ʔsleŋ, “twinkling stars”) + phonetic 生 (OC *sʰleːŋ, *sreŋs). 晶 originally referred to this word; a phonetic 生 was added later (Ji Xusheng, 2004). 晶 was later simplified into 日.
Baxter and Sagart (2014) reconstructs the Old Chinese as *s-tsʰˤeŋ, which can be analysed as a verbal root *tsʰˤeŋ (“bright”) with a prefix *s-. This reconstruction accounts for the Min initial *tsh- and the use of the character to write the word 晴 (OC *N-tsʰeŋ).
Possibly related to 清 (OC *sʰleŋ, “clear”) (Schuessler, 2007; Baxter and Sagart, 2014), in turn from Proto-Sino-Tibetan *(t)s(j)aŋ (“clear; pure; clean”).
Proto-Kiranti *saŋ (“star”) either develops from a parallel Sino-Tibetan root (Schuessler, 2007) or derives from Proto-Sino-Tibetan *sV-kar (“star”) (STEDT).

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 形義通解；字形分析與用例
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 星 as 从晶、生聲: 晶 depicts an array of stars and 生 is the phonetic. It reports the original sense as stars, a Western Zhou bronze inscription 麓伯簋 using 星 in a personal name, and an oracle-bone example 合集15625反 read as “晴” (clear weather). It also cites 星言夙駕 in the Shijing as clear-weather use, but that interpretation is disputed. The entry records later borrowing of 星 for 腥 in Warring States/Qin slips and Han silk manuscripts, and extensions such as scattered or numerous. These attestations do not establish a precise first-occurrence date for each sense.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：甲骨部件分析—晶

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 《說文》 account; 晶 entry
evidence.text: The entry quotes the Shuowen analysis 从晶，生聲 and its alternative pictographic explanation, then treats 晶 as an earlier spelling for the star word. It also describes later 晶 senses such as bright, clear, and crystal. This is the dictionary's historical interpretation; the detailed sequence is not settled by the text alone.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：甲骨部件分析—晶

evidence.source: 《說文解字》, transcribed in the CUHK historical dictionary entry
evidence.field: phonetic component 生; reading comparison
evidence.text: The entry identifies 生 as 星's phonetic component. The supplied local Baxter–Sagart rows (sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv; rows for 星 and 生) give 星 MC seng, OC *s-tsʰˤeŋ and 生 MC sraeng, OC *sreŋ (with listed variants/notes). Those same-system local rows show a sound relationship to assess, but do not independently prove the historical phonetic function. The official reconstruction-table PDF could not be opened in this session. Supplied local Unihan rows (sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt; kMandarin rows for 星 and 生) give xīng and shēng; official per-character Unicode pages could not be inspected, so these values are not asserted as externally verified here.

evidence.field: 字形演變
evidence.text: The page catalogs oracle-bone forms, a Western Zhou bronze inscription, Warring States forms, seal forms, and later scripts. Its explanation says the two displayed oracle-bone examples combine a star depiction with 生, while some Warring States forms simplify 晶 and retain 生 as phonetic; it describes reduction of the star depiction to 日. This account differs from the attached 《說文新證》 note on another inspected page, which says a 晶-only form preceded the addition of 生. The text view does not resolve whether these concern different early forms or competing analyses; no glyph image was visually inspected in this pass.

context.provenance: Base evidence consists of imported local JSONL excerpts. Source names identify upstream datasets; extraction may lose sense and language boundaries. Further external evidence and research activity are documented separately in the dossier.
editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

items.period: Shang oracle-script style; modern digital redraw based on catalogued form HB2813
items.caption: This oracle-style 星 form has a tall central stroke with short branches and several surrounding enclosed marks. It is presented as a modern redraw of a catalogued Shang-style form; interpretations of how the star-like element and 生 relate in the earliest forms differ.
items.alt: Black oracle-style glyph with a tall branched central shape and four separate enclosed marks around it.
items.selection_reason: The visible form is legible and relevant to 星’s early graphic history. It helps show the form discussed in accounts that connect 星 with a star depiction and 生, while leaving the disputed early sequence open.
items.rights: Public-domain release for the SVG representation, as stated on the Commons file page.

limitations.text: This is a modern digital redraw, not an image of an excavated object. Early accounts disagree on whether oracle forms already combined star imagery with 生 or whether a 晶-based form preceded 星 with 生; the sequence remains unsettled.
